summary: Status page not reflecting embeddings failures (request for dedicated Embeddings component + per-region visibility)
description:
Customer reports repeated 5xx/timeout errors on Embeddings API while public status page showed "All Systems Operational" for Hosted API.

Customer context
- Company: Northbridge AI Platform (enterprise)
- Workload: embeddings batch + online queries (vector search), latency-sensitive
- Integration: Redwood REST API via internal SDK
- Region: us-east (primary)

Issue summary (customer)
- From ~2025-11-07 21:18 UTC to ~22:05 UTC, customer observed elevated Embeddings failures (HTTP 500/502/504 + timeouts).
- Status page did not show an Embeddings-specific component or any degraded state.
- Customer request: add a dedicated Embeddings component (and ideally per-region) so they can programmatically gate traffic and communicate internally.

Impact (customer-stated)
- ~8–12% of embeddings requests failed (mix of 5xx + timeouts).
- Downstream impact: delayed indexing jobs and partial search result degradation.

Steps to reproduce / evidence
- Endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings
- Example request ID(s) (from customer):
  - req_01HFK9V3Y7WQ2QZ5N2Q8X0JQ3A
  - req_01HFK9V5KAXP0F8C9S4P5K2M1R
- Example timestamps (UTC):
  - 2025-11-07 21:23:41Z
  - 2025-11-07 21:31:10Z
  - 2025-11-07 21:48:05Z

Customer-provided error samples
1) HTTP 504
- message: upstream timeout
- duration_ms: ~30000
- region: us-east

2) HTTP 502
- message: gateway error
- response headers included: x-redwood-region=us-east

3) SDK error
- "ReadTimeout: timed out while awaiting headers" (client timeout 30s)

Ask
- Confirm whether Redwood had an incident or partial outage affecting embeddings in us-east.
- Explain why status page did not reflect the embeddings impact.
- Provide timeline + publishable summary they can share internally.
- Roadmap/ETA for embeddings component granularity on the public status page.
comments: 2025-11-08 09:12 UTC — Dev Patel (Support) — Opened on behalf of Northbridge after escalation from CSM. Pulling request IDs + checking internal dashboards. Looping in #incidents and SRE on-call for verification.

2025-11-08 09:41 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE) — Initial triage: we did have a localized degradation in us-east affecting a subset of inference traffic. Our current public components are too coarse ("Hosted API") and the status thresholds are primarily error-rate based at the aggregate gateway level. If embeddings errors were misclassified or diluted by other traffic, component status may not have flipped. Investigating request IDs now.

2025-11-08 10:03 UTC — Allison Grant (Observability) — Found elevated embeddings error counters in us-east between 21:20–22:05 UTC. Looks like errors were being labeled under generic route="/v1" in some cases (missing capability tag), which would undercount the embeddings-specific panel. Related to ongoing metric tagging work; see gateway metrics tagging PR workstream.

Root contributor appears to be a transient backend saturation event plus retries amplifying p95/p99 latency. We did not publish a public incident at the time; the incident channel focused on streaming degradation (INC-2025-1107-STREAM-US-EAST-DEGRADED) and we treated embeddings as part of the broader "Hosted API" bucket. This is the exact gap the Status Page Transparency Upgrades initiative is addressing.

2025-11-08 10:38 UTC — Dev Patel (Support) — Sent interim response to customer: acknowledged mismatch, confirmed us-east embeddings impact window, and committed to follow up with a publishable summary + planned improvements (embeddings component). 2025-11-08 11:10 UTC — Christine Wong (SRE/Status transparency) — This aligns with customer requests we’ve been tracking: add Embeddings as a first-class component and split by region. They require a status page component that explicitly references Embeddings, and they prefer updates within 15 minutes for customer-visible incidents.

2025-11-09 09:30 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE) — Provided draft publishable summary for Support/CS review (no sensitive capacity details): timeframe, region, symptom, mitigation, and prevention. Notes: we can’t promise 15-minute updates as an SLA, but we can share our internal target (time-to-first-update) as a process improvement goal.

2025-11-10 16:15 UTC — Michael Grant (Legal) — Reviewed draft language (via CS). Approved with minor edits: avoid specific utilization/capacity phrasing; keep it to 'elevated errors and timeouts' and 'traffic management and stabilization changes'.

2025-11-12 10:05 UTC — Dev Patel (Support) — Sent final response to customer including (1) confirmed window + region, (2) explanation of why status page didn’t show embeddings (component granularity + signal labeling), and (3) remediation plan (taxonomy update + signal mapping + anti-flap thresholds). Customer acknowledged and asked to be notified when Embeddings component is live. Marking ticket resolved; leaving open follow-up via CS for rollout notification.
resolution: Confirmed an us-east embeddings degradation window (2025-11-07 ~21:18–22:05 UTC) that was not reflected on the public status page due to coarse component taxonomy (Embeddings not a first-class component) and incomplete capability labeling/roll-up for customer-facing signals. Support provided a publishable, non-sensitive summary to the customer and linked the gap to the in-flight Status Page Transparency Upgrades initiative. Follow-ups: implement dedicated Embeddings component + per-region breakdown where supported; improve metric tagging and component mapping validation; incorporate into weekly status accuracy audits.
